clue.text: Water may get through these doors and into the locks

definitions.text: Water may get through these doors and into the locks

parts.words: Water may get through these doors and into the locks
parts.note: describes sluice doors on a canal or river that let water pass and fill the chambers of a lock; 'locks' teases hair before it settles on canals

explanation.surface: A warning that water can seep under the doors and reach the door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluices on a waterway are opened to let water flow into a canal lock chamber.

clue.text: Dislike hotel with a licence

indicators.note: taking licence with the letters means treating them freely, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a hotel that holds a drinks licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licence' rearranges HOTEL and A; it looks like a drinks licence.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate intensely is to dislike strongly, a verb.

clue.text: Primordial queer fish

definitions.meaning: an eccentric or odd person, an unusual character

explanation.surface: Ancient primitive fish of a strange kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: earliest, first in time; and a person of unusual, eccentric character.

clue.text: Coquette who wheedled money-out of a man of 49?

definitions.meaning: a flirt who coaxes wealth from men
a Forty-Niner, a prospector in the 1849 California rush

explanation.surface: A flirt charms cash from a middle-aged man of forty-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: '49' looks like an age; it is the year 1849 of the California gold rush, whose miners were Forty-Niners.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a woman chasing men for their wealth, and a prospector seeking precious metal in 1849 California.

clue.text: Diet, say, peculiar to a Scottish region

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, signalling the letters of diet and say are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A certain diet is said to be special to one part of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A former local-government region of eastern Scotland around the River Tay.

clue.text: Author needed a drink

definitions.meaning: the pen name of H. H. Munro, Edwardian short-story writer
a variant spelling of sake, Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A writer needed a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the pen name of short-story writer H. H. Munro, and a Japanese rice wine spelt differently.

clue.text: The law of the world in abbreviated form

definitions.text: The law of the world in abbreviated form

parts.words: The law of the world in abbreviated form
parts.note: the global police organisation, the 'law' as police, whose name is a shortening of its full title

explanation.surface: International law written in a short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The International Criminal Police Organization, known by a shortened name, is policing on a world scale.

clue.text: Reckless men dread posse becoming involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled, signalling the letters of dread and posse get mixed up

explanation.surface: Reckless men fear the sheriff's posse joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold outlaws of the Wild West, desperate and reckless characters.

clue.text: A rendezvous in Broadway say?

parts.note: a rendezvous is a meeting place, a venue

explanation.surface: Someone arranges to meet a date somewhere on Broadway.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is an example of a wide city street, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Agents to assemble outside on ethnic lines

indicators.note: the gathering word is placed outside, around the agency's letters

parts.note: to rally is to gather or assemble
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, staffed by agents

explanation.surface: Spies gather outside to organise along ethnic divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Done on ethnic lines means divided according to race, an adverb matching the answer.

clue.text: Shallow bark going to sea

parts.note: bark is the skin of a tree
the deep is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: A small boat heads out into shallow waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' looks like a boat (barque) or a dog's noise; it is a tree's outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superficial, only on the surface, is called shallow.

clue.text: Plant appearing right in the morass

indicators.note: the right letter goes inside the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is a marsh or morass

explanation.surface: A plant is seen growing on the right side of a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracken-like frond-bearing plant of damp places.

clue.text: Nominal leader is responsible for carving on ship

definitions.meaning: a leader in name only without real power
a carved bust or figure at the prow of a sailing ship

explanation.surface: A leader in name takes credit for the carvings on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a powerless leader in title only, and a carved statue at a vessel's bow.

clue.text: Popular nappy containing a soft absorbent material

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the nappy word holds the letter A within it

parts.note: diaper is the American word for a nappy
P is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A fashionable nappy is made of soft absorbent stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAPER (American for nappy) holds A and P (piano, soft) to give DIAPAPER, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: India paper is a thin, soft, absorbent printing paper.

clue.text: Great hotel renovated completely

indicators.note: renovated means rebuilt, so the letters of great and hotel are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A grand hotel has been totally refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly, entirely, in total: a synonym adverb.

clue.text: George has record year in science

parts.note: Geo. is an abbreviation of the name George
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: George has broken a record in a scientific field this year.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of the earth's rocks and structure is a branch of science.

clue.text: Hunter, for example, is an experienced person

definitions.meaning: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover, an old timepiece
a veteran who has been around a long time

explanation.surface: A huntsman is described as a seasoned person.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a pocket watch with a lid over its face, not a huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a veteran with long experience, and an antique timekeeper such as a hunter watch.

clue.text: In the station, bay horse was first to be accommodated

parts.note: in racing form, b stands for a bay horse
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: A bay horse arrived first at the station and was given lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Racecards abbreviate a horse's colour, so B means bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse put up in stalls is housed or lodged.

clue.text: Uncomplimentary remark from loyal chap on striker

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, loyal person
a bat is something you strike a ball with

explanation.surface: A rude comment from a loyal fellow about a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer; it is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A critical comment or insult, figuratively something thrown at someone.

clue.text: Complex apparent in many English

parts.note: divers is an old word for several or many

explanation.surface: A complex is evident in many English people.
explanation.definitionFit: Varied and of many kinds, hence intricate or complicated.

clue.text: Communist woman's symbol of marriage an irrelevant diversion

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
her is the possessive for a woman
a wedding ring symbolises marriage

explanation.surface: A Communist woman's wedding ring distracts from the real issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue that draws attention away from the truth is a distraction in a mystery story.

clue.text: Students in the island causing complaints

indicators.note: the learners sit inside the island letters

parts.note: Is. is the abbreviation for island
L is a learner, so LL is two learners or students

explanation.surface: Students on an island cause trouble and grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments or troubles, the sense of complaints as illnesses.

clue.text: Messenger abbreviated nothing, without interruption

indicators.note: shortened, so the envoy word loses its final letter

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or papal messenger
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A messenger cut his report short, saying nothing without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' cuts the last letter from LEGATE, leaving LEGAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning smoothly, with the notes joined.

clue.text: Fine crack in musical row

parts.note: Hair is a famous 1960s rock musical
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A dispute over a row of seats at a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin fracture, as in a cup or bone, is described this way.

clue.text: S. American king incarcerated at the outset

indicators.note: the opening letters of incarcerated are taken

explanation.surface: A South American ruler was imprisoned from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sapa Inca was the emperor of the Andean empire, so a South American ruler.

clue.text: Tramp surrounded by a lot of paper and bottles

definitions.note: the clue gives a plural; the answer is one large bottle size, so the plural is loose

indicators.note: the tramp word is placed inside the paper word

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper
hobo is an American word for a tramp

explanation.surface: A vagrant is found among heaps of paper and empty bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural but the answer is a single bottle size, a looseness of the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is an oversized wine bottle holding six standard ones.

clue.text: Without a shilling, would be very sparing of vinegar

indicators.note: the letter for shilling is removed from the austere word

parts.note: ascetic means austere and very sparing in comfort
S is the abbreviation for shilling, the old British coin

explanation.surface: A miser without a shilling would be stingy with the vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from ASCETIC leaves ACETIC. A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the sour compound in vinegar, so the adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Breach of rules by bear switching share

indicators.note: the letters of bear are switched around into a new order

parts.note: a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A bear switching its share of food breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' rearranges BEAR to ABER, then RATION follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A deviation from the normal or correct course is a departure from rules.
